title: Rapid escalation: priority-slab smoothing & prefetch-credit leak remediation for TTFT spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Multiple enterprise customers (one Hosted PLG customer, two Dedicated/Private clusters) reported sudden increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and token/sec collapse for models with >16k context. The spike correlates with ~2025-11-11 kernel selection heuristic rollout and an unrelated prefetch credit accounting change rolled last week. Impact: interactive latency regressions, client timeouts, and customer escalations to Support/AE.

Root cause hypothesis (triage):
- Under bursty multi-tenant workloads, the kernel selector occasionally chooses a quant-optimized execution path that expects a warm KV cache. That path triggers aggressive prefetching and consumes tenant-prefetch credits.
- A race in prefetch-credit accounting (introduced in last sprint) fails to restore credits when a kernel fallback happens, leaving tenants effectively starved of prefetch budget.
- Prefetch-starvation increases cold prefix work and causes kernel warmup cascades across multiplexed streams, amplifying TTFT for affected tenants.
- Private clusters show higher severity due to tighter tenant isolation and lower shared warmup amplification.

Mitigation plan (short term):
1) Emergency mitigation push (today): revert the specific prefetch-credit accounting change server-side via feature flag. This reduces credit leakage immediately.
2) Introduce a temporary per-tenant reserve bucket (grace credits) that guarantees a small amount of prefetch capacity when credit accounting inconsistency is detected.
3) Add an immediate kernel-selection fallback: if a chosen kernel triggers a large prefetch without sufficient verified credits, instant fallback to conservative kernel with no prefetch and short-circuit metric to telemetry.
4) Monitoring: create dashboards for per-tenant prefetch utilization, kernel-fallback rate, TTFT P50/P95, and tokens/sec. Alert thresholds for sudden uplift in falls back >5x baseline.

Permanent fixes (next sprint):
- Correct atomicity of prefetch-credit restore (race fix) with unit + fuzz tests.
- Implement bounded prefetch heuristics that account for multiplexed stream headroom.
- Add long-term signal for kernel selector to prefer conservative kernels during cold-start spikes.

Rollout plan:
- Step 0 (hotfix): Feature-flag revert deployed to Hosted within 30m of triage; Dedicated/Private edge patches scheduled same-day with ops coordination.
- Step 1 (canary): Deploy kernel fallback + grace credits to 5% of Hosted traffic + one low-risk Dedicated customer cluster (non-production) for 4 hours.
- Step 2 (ramp): 25% -> 75% -> 100% over 24 hours if TTFT and tokens/sec metrics stabilize.
- Step 3 (postmortem & permanent fix): Implement race fix and bounded heuristics in runtime-1.20 patch release.

Instrumentation and validation:
- Added synthetic probes simulating multi-tenant bursts with long-context prompts to validate fallback behavior.
- New dashboards: /dashboards/runtime/prefetch-credit-leak and /dashboards/runtime/kernel-fallbacks.

Customer communication:
- Support/AE notified customers with preliminary root-cause and immediate mitigation actions. Scheduled 1:1 for impacted enterprise customers.
- Public status page updates included summary, ETA for regression fix, and mitigation steps.

Artifacts & links:
- Runbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-834212+prefetch-credit-leak
- Repo PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1924
- Canary config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/commit/7a1f2b3
- Customer incident thread (Support): https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/834212-thread

Open trade-offs considered:
- Option A (aggressive): Disable prefetch entirely for bursty tenants — reduces TTFT but increases per-token compute cost (higher unit cost). Rejected for immediate rollout because cost impact on hosters could be large.
- Option B (conservative): Implement per-tenant grace credits + kernel fallback — chosen because it balances latency relief and cost exposure while being quick to deploy.

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- TTFT P95 for impacted tenants returns to baseline within 6 hours of full ramp.
- No increase in error rates or out-of-memory events after fallback rollout.
- Code changes merged with unit/fuzz tests and a postmortem published within 72 hours.
